facts.text: Riverside is the first planned suburb in the United States, designed in 1869 by landscape architects Calvert Vaux and Frederick Law Olmsted.
The Riverside Landscape Architecture District, bounded by 26th Street, Harlem and Ogden avenues, the Des Plaines River, and Golf Road, earned National Historic Landmark status in 1970.
A new historical plaque from the Illinois State Historical Society was unveiled in 2025, detailing Riverside’s origins as one of America’s first planned suburbs.
The Riverside train station, former Henninger’s Pharmacy, and the Sidney Allen home at 84 Riverside Road served as filming locations for the movie The Lake House.
Riverside’s early civic life featured the 1893 Golf Club, the 1895 Chateauesque Township Hall, and the 1901 Burlington line train station.
The village of Riverside was officially incorporated in 1875, just six years after its founding.
